files.content: # Watercolour — Style Prompt > A hand-painted journal page that paints itself: translucent washes and dry-brush strokes on warm cotton paper, a striped vermilion sun, one hand-drawn ink horizon, a quiet serif title and small mono measurements. The world arrives as a wash swept in from the left with a stepped brush edge, trees paint themselves trunk first, the camera walks slowly along one continuous painted land whose colours change with the place, and paper-coloured mist washes it all back to a blank page. ## 1. Essence, and what it is not - **One sheet of warm, fibrous paper** under everything. It is also the eraser: paper-coloured mist washes things away. - **Everything painted is brush strokes and washes**: a variable-width ribbon at partial opacity plus a few thin bristle tracks that break into dashes (flying white); washes overlap and darken where they cross, like transparent pigment. There are no vector outlines. The only lines are ink: the horizon, trunks and branches, a pen leader to a note. - **Things paint themselves in, structure before detail**: trunk, then crown; the land as horizontal washes from the left; the lake from its middle outward. - **A journal's annotation layer**: a serif title and subtitles, a chapter counter, a small measured value on a scale, a hand note on a pen leader. - **One world, one camera**: chapters are places along the same painted land, reached by walking, not by cutting. - Tone: calm, curious, precise. Numbers are real; the palette can carry the data. Not ink wash (colour, not ink tones; no calligraphic gesture), not impasto (no thick paint), not a children's picture book (no crayon, no cute outlines), not vector illustration with a watercolour texture laid on top, not a slideshow of unrelated pictures. ## 2. Materials & rendering - **Paper**: the `--latar` ground plus one static texture painted at load at half resolution: two octaves of smooth mottling (about ±3-5 % value), ~1,800 short curved fibres at 3-7 % opacity, and a vignette about 6 % darker in the corners. It lies under the painting and never moves; the washes are translucent, so the grain shows through them. - **Stroke** (`kuas`): a ribbon along a curve whose width follows a profile (brush, leaf, flat, trunk) with ±22 % value-noise roughness, its body at 0.58 × the stroke's opacity, plus 1-8 bristle tracks at 30-85 % opacity, each with its own dash pattern and an early end: that is the flying white. - **Wash** (`cat`): the same polygon filled three times with its vertices jittered 2-6 px, a third of the opacity each, then a 2 px rim at 30 %: soft, ragged edges with a faint pooled line. - **Depth by three parallax layers**: far ridges (0.35×, palest, their feet lost in a paper-coloured mist band, the sky tint above them painted into the same layer), mid stepped bands at the horizon (0.6×, three ragged washes, distant small trees), near ground below the ink line (1×, two wash passes, a darker band along the line, ~320 short horizontal dry-brush streaks, fading to paper in the bottom third). - **Hero objects** (trees, grass tufts, a rock, a lake, a forest band, a tent) are small canvases painted once from a seeded PRNG and revealed by `clip-path`; nothing is redrawn per frame. Soft layers are painted at lower resolution (far ridges ½, mid bands and ground ¾, mist ¼). - **Page furniture** fixed to the sheet, not the world: the sun (a 120 px disc, three-pass wash, nine darker horizontal brush stripes clipped inside, a 5 px ring of unpainted paper) and the ink horizon (y 741, 3-4 px, its width varying by hand). - No live 3D, no filters, no blend modes, no gradients standing in for paint. ## 3. Colour logic - `--latar` is the paper. Light is unpainted paper; the mist is `--latar`; nothing is painted pure white. - `--utama` is the one vermilion accent that recurs: the sun, the red rock, the tent, the chapter dash, the brush stroke behind the price. Its tints are the dry land: `--tanah` (28 % of `--utama` in slightly inked paper with a fixed ochre), `--jauh` for far ridges (17 %), `--batu` for the rock (80 %). - `--aksen` is the rain blue: the measurement bar and drop marker, the water (`--air`, 64 % in paper) and the cool hills (`--bukit`, 28 %). - The sky stays paper at the top and takes a tint near the horizon (up to 14 %): `--utama` over the dry land, `--air` toward the water, so it warms and cools with the place. - `--teks` is the ink of titles, subtitles and notes; `--tinta` (62 % `--teks`, 38 % `--utama`) is the reddish-brown ink of the horizon, trunks and pen leaders; `--teks-redup` carries chapter counters, labels and italic sublines; `--teks-di-utama` is the price on the brush stroke. - **Palette as data**: ground, mid bands and ridges change colour with place in five quantised bands (dry ochre → sage), each band its own ragged wash overlapping the next, so the seams read as wet edges. Never a smooth gradient, never a straight vertical seam. - Fixed hues, mixed into the brand's paper or ink so they follow light and dark brands: leaves #868a72, dark leaves #545b46, dry grass #a8975a, forest #587052. Keep 3-5 hues per scene plus ink. - On a dark brand the paper is dark and the ink light; the washes still mix toward `--latar`, so the painting reads as the same place at night. ## 4. Type - `--font-judul` (Cormorant Garamond 500, upright and italic) carries every voice: the title in italic at 120 px centred around y 380; the chapter name upright at 64 px; the measured figure upright at 58 px; subtitles in italic at 42 px centred at the bottom (from y 902); notes in italic at 36 px; the tracked subline in caps at 22 px, 0.36 em, `--teks-redup`. Serif text over paint carries a paper-coloured halo (`text-shadow` 8 px and 20 px of `--latar`). - `--font-isi` (IBM Plex Mono 400) carries measurements: the chapter counter at 20 px, 0.3 em; the scale label in caps at 18 px, 0.3 em; tick numbers at 16 px; the second subtitle line at 22 px, 0.12 em. - Without brand fonts: Cormorant Garamond, Libre Baskerville or Playfair Display italic for the serif; IBM Plex Mono or Inter for labels. A wider brand font wraps sooner: shorten the subtitle, keep its size. - Numbers as digits with Indonesian thousands (1.420), units in lower case after the figure. ## 5. Motion quality - **Painting-in is the main motion.** The ink horizon draws left to right in 0.9 s (`power2.inOut`). Title letters appear 0.05 s apart, each fading in 0.16 s; the subline follows 0.9 s after the first letter, the small line 0.25 s later (0.6 s fades), the subtitle 0.4 s. - **The wash wipe** takes 1.6 s, quad in-out. Each layer is cut into 30 px bands; each band's front lags 0-0.19 of the move (smooth noise plus jitter) and its end wobbles ±18-30 px. The far layer trails by 0.08 and the mid layer by 0.04, so the edge is stepped and layered. The title fades out (0.6 s) while the wash comes in. - **Trees**: the trunk reveals bottom to top in 0.42 s, the crown opens as a circle from its base in 0.6 s starting 0.3 s later; trees 0.3 s apart. Tufts 0.35 s, staggered by their place along the land. The rock opens left to right in 0.6 s, the lake from its centre in 0.9 s (`power2.out`), the far forest left to right in 0.9 s (a burst stays under 1 s). - **Sway** only after painting: crowns skew by 0.55° sin(1.15 t + φ) + 0.22° sin(2.7 t + 2φ). - **Margin notes**: the chapter block fades in 0.5 s, the measure 0.2 s later; the bar grows from zero in 1 s (`power2.out`) while the figure counts and the drop marker slides; the subtitle fades in 0.4 s. All leave together in 0.3 s (`power1.in`) before the camera moves on. A pen leader draws in 0.4 s, then its note writes left to right in 0.55 s. - **Mist** rises in 0.95 s (`power1.inOut`) with a 300 px soft wavy edge built from eight steps of 16 %. - Reading text holds at least 2.5 s; the end card is still for at least 2 s. ## 6. Camera grammar Parallax: far 0.35×, mid 0.6×, near 1×. The sun, the ink horizon, titles and margin notes stay on the page. | Move | What it expresses | Can serve | |---|---|---| | Locked sheet, things painted in | study, attention | a title page, a specimen plate, a recipe card | | Brush-edge wash from the left | a new entry painted onto the page | opening the first chapter, a new day | | Slow lateral walk (120 px/s, linear, never stopping between chapters) | the journey goes on; the world is continuous | any chapter hold, a route, a timeline | | Long walk (1,700 px in 1.3 s, quad in-out) over the same land while its colours change | crossing to the next place; a gradient in space | dry to wet, city to village, before to after | | Slow push into a detail (1 → 1.12 over 3 s) | the observer leaning in | a seed, a stamp, a handwritten note | | Paper mist rising | chapter end, time passing, forgetting | the ending, a season, leaving a place | Framing: generous paper margins (120 px at the sides), one hero subject per view with its note, labels never over the subject. Transitions are washes, mist or the walk itself: no hard cuts, no dissolves between unrelated pictures. ## 7. Native moves - **The title page.** Blank paper, the sun already on the page, an ink horizon drawn across, the title written letter by letter, a tracked subline, a two-line subtitle at the foot. *Fits content like:* the first page of a trip diary; a cooking class's recipe journal; a creator's series opener; the opening of a short fairy tale. - **Brush-edge wash.** The next place is painted in from the left in stepped, layered bands while the title fades. *Fits content like:* day one of a tour; the first module of a course; a homestay's garden appearing; a new chapter of a story. - **Painting-in as reveal.** Each subject paints itself as it arrives, structure first: trunk, then crown; outline wash, then detail. *Fits content like:* the plants of a nursery; the stages of a pottery workshop; the ingredients of a dish; a character entering a story. - **Measured margin note.** Top right, a mono label, a serif figure that counts, a short scale with a coloured bar and a drop marker sliding to the value. *Fits content like:* kilometres walked; altitude reached; rainfall on a farm; minutes of practice in a class; subscribers gained on a channel. - **Palette as data.** The camera walks along one land whose washes change colour band by band. *Fits content like:* dry season to rainy season on a farm; a river from source to sea; a neighbourhood before and after a clean-up; a mood shifting through a story. - **Specimen and note.** One subject with a serif note on a pen leader. *Fits content like:* where the tent stands; the best seat in a café; the part of a bicycle a repair class fixes; the clue in a mystery. - **Mist to the end card.** Paper mist rises and erases the world back to the title page; the name is written, the price lands on a vermilion brush stroke, the contact sits in the subtitle line. *Fits content like:* a tour's booking card; a class's enrolment card; a creator's channel sign-off; "the end" of a story. ## 8. Pitfalls - **Performance (live preview).** Paint every canvas once at load from a seeded PRNG, then turn it into an `` (`Object.assign(new Image(), { decoding: "sync", src: canvas.toDataURL() })`): a canvas element is re-composited from its full bitmap every frame, an image is rasterised once into its layer. Then only translate layers or animate `clip-path` on small images. Never redraw per frame, never animate a filter or blur, keep the paper a static layer under the painting, and hide (`autoAlpha: 0`) scenes and the mist while they are not on screen. Composite only what moves (`will-change: transform` on the camera layers and the swaying crowns, not on every sprite). Paint soft layers at lower resolution so the page still loads quickly on a slow phone. - **Checks.** Set generated image sources with `Object.assign` as above and keep `url(` and `src=` out of the script text: the composition check reads them as remote files. - **Colours in canvas.** Canvas needs real colours: resolve each token through a probe element's computed colour and a 1×1 canvas (this resolves `color-mix`), so the painting follows the brand with no colour written in script. - **Seams.** A translucent wash that ends inside the frame shows a hard seam: extend washes past their canvas and fade the bottom to paper with `destination-out`. A hill polygon that starts at full height shows a vertical cut: ramp it up from its foot. Smooth gradients and gradient stops read as software: use ragged, overlapping bands. - **Mechanical edges.** A wipe with straight, evenly stepped cuts looks like a staircase: vary band lags with smooth noise plus jitter, wobble each band end, and let the far layers trail. - **Trees that read as palms.** Crown strands rise steeply (±0.75 rad from vertical) and only droop at their tips, more the more they lean; drooping all around gives a coconut palm. - **Text over paint.** Subtitles sit over the ground wash: keep the paper halo and the ground fading lighter toward the bottom. Tiny mono labels belong only on the sky. Keep the measure block clear of the sun (from x 1550). - **Brands.** On a pale brand (pale main on white) the land is a faint wash; the ink and the rim of the sun still separate it from the paper. Never mix the paper toward `--utama` for text surfaces. - **Safe zones** at 16:9: 120 px left and right, 80 px top and bottom; subtitles about ten words at most. ## Measured from the references - Rhythm of the reference opening: blank paper with the sun and horizon for ~0.7 s; the title writes over ~0.75 s (~0.05 s a letter); subline at ~1.5 s; subtitle at ~2.2 s; held ~6 s; the title fades over ~0.5 s while the wash wipes in from the left in ~0.9 s; the chapter header follows ~0.3 s later; trees paint over ~1 s; the camera walks about 8 % of the frame width per second. - Layout at 1920 × 1080: horizon at y 741 (68.6 %); sun centred at (1464, 249), radius 60; title centred around y 400; header at the top-left margin, measure at top right ending at the right margin; a two-line subtitle at the foot (the example lifts it to y 902-1000 for the safe zone). - Colours: paper #f0e9d9 in the centre, #e1dacd in the corners; sun #d8623f; ink horizon #63473c; ground #dcac88 under the horizon to #ddbea3 at the foot; mid bands #dfb293; far ridges #e0cab4; rain blue #4f7491.

# Watercolour: beat plan

Default length 15 s. Tempo per beat (seconds): short 2.2, medium 3.2, long 4.5.

## hook

- en: blank paper and a striped vermilion sun; an ink horizon is drawn and the serif title writes itself letter by letter
- id: kertas kosong dan matahari merah bata; garis cakrawala ditarik, judul serif tertulis huruf demi huruf

## problem

- en: the land paints in dry and pale; a serif note on a pen leader points at what is missing
- id: tanah terlukis kering dan pucat; catatan bertali pena menunjuk apa yang kurang

## fact

- en: one subject paints itself stroke by stroke, trunk before leaves, with a serif note on a pen leader
- id: satu objek melukis diri sapuan demi sapuan, batang dulu baru daun, dengan catatan bertali pena

## step

- en: a wash sweeps in from the left with a stepped brush edge; chapter number, name and the painted subject follow
- id: sapuan cat masuk dari kiri bertepi kuas bertangga; nomor bab, nama, dan objek yang dilukis menyusul

## compare

- en: the camera walks along one painted land; its washes change colour band by band from one end to the other
- id: kamera berjalan di satu lukisan; warna catnya berganti pita demi pita dari ujung ke ujung

## number

- en: a measure top right: the serif figure counts, a blue bar grows on a small scale, a drop marker slides along
- id: angka ukur di kanan atas: angka serif dihitung, batang biru tumbuh di skala kecil, penanda tetes bergeser

## proof

- en: a still plate: the subject painted whole, small labels on pen leaders naming its parts
- id: halaman diam: objek dilukis utuh, label kecil bertali pena menamai bagian-bagiannya

## offer

- en: on blank paper the offer is written in serif, then a vermilion brush stroke lands behind the price
- id: di kertas kosong penawaran ditulis serif, lalu sapuan kuas merah bata mendarat di belakang harga

## cta

- en: paper mist rises and erases the world; name, price on a brush stroke and contact are written, held 2 s
- id: kabut kertas naik menghapus lukisan; nama, harga di atas sapuan cat, dan kontak tertulis, diam 2 detik

## payoff

- en: the finished painting holds by the sun; one last accent stroke lands under the key word, held 2 s
- id: lukisan yang selesai diam di bawah matahari; satu sapuan aksen terakhir mendarat di kata kunci, diam 2 detik
